note: Independent rejudge against RFC 2866 Section 3 ("The Request Authenticator field in Accounting-Request packets contains a one-way MD5 hash calculated over a stream of octets consisting of the Code + Identifier + Length + 16 zero octets + request attributes + shared secret (where + indicates concatenation)."). TestRFC2866SentAccountingRequestCarriesTheSection3Authenticator changed only a comment (Exchange->exchange in 69f3e72365); it captures the Accounting-Request put on the wire by SendToServers/exchange/encodeRequest and asserts exact equality with independent MD5(Code+ID+Length+16 zeros+attributes+secret) and inequality with pkt.Authenticator. TestRFC2866AccountingRequestAuthFormula proves zero-substitution over garbage bytes, and TestRFC2866AccountingRequestAuthRejectsTampering proves sensitivity to secret, attribute bytes, and Code. Verdict enforced stands.
